backup.production_rule: Purely additive: one nullable column on staff_access_profiles. No existing column, policy or grant is touched, so the 06:14Z backup set taken earlier today remains a valid restore point.

forward_verification.name: note_column_exists_as_nullable_text
forward_verification.query: select exists (select 1 from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='staff_access_profiles' and column_name='note' and data_type='text' and is_nullable='YES')

forward_verification.name: no_existing_row_lost_its_role
forward_verification.query: select not exists (select 1 from public.staff_access_profiles where role is null)

forward_verification.name: column_carries_the_no_credentials_warning
forward_verification.query: select col_description('public.staff_access_profiles'::regclass, (select ordinal_position from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='staff_access_profiles' and column_name='note')::int) like '%Never store a PIN%'

steps.name: drop_the_column
steps.action: alter table public.staff_access_profiles drop column note; no other object depends on it, and the edge function tolerates its absence by returning null.

feature_flags.name: staff_note_field
feature_flags.required_state: not a runtime flag - the column is inert until the staff-users edge function and the admin dashboard are deployed to read and write it. Applying this migration alone changes nothing user-facing.

compatibility.evidence: ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS on a nullable text column. Existing readers select named columns and are unaffected; existing writers never referenced it. The current staff-users function does not read or write note, so deploying the migration before the function is safe and the reverse order is safe too.

stop_conditions: any forward verification query returns anything other than its expected value
the note column must never be used to store a PIN or password - it is not protected to credential standard and the column comment says so
